headline: Pretrained foundation models for DNA, RNA, protein, and single-cell sequence data
label: Biological Sequence Foundation Models
summary: Benchmarks now test whether biological sequence foundation models generalize under cross-experiment shift, long context, and quantization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretraining large models on biological sequences (DNA, RNA, protein, peptide, and single-cell data) and evaluating them against task-specific baselines. RIBOSPAN, a 1.61B-parameter bidirectional RNA model pretrained to 10,240 nt, and GB.GeneUnet, an 837M-parameter transformer U-Net extending gene expression prediction to 1 Mb, push context length. Evaluation is becoming more stringent: the scAraFM study reports inflated random-split performance relative to cross-experiment splits, and the GenomeOcean FP8 study finds biological fidelity largely preserved while realized speedups diverge from theoretical ones. Cross-modal pretraining with proteomics data matches or beats larger RNA-only single-cell models, and Monroe applies in-context probabilistic inference to molecules. Compact alternatives also remain competitive: a BiLSTM peptide autoencoder matches pLM performance with interpretable latent spaces, and single-cell benchmarks report that the best scLMs use minimal count processing.
